title: Pilot qualifier: embeddings + cache mini playbook
body:
Purpose:
A compact sales enablement + battlecard style note for sellers running embedding-first pilots where cost and latency are front-and-center. This doc is intentionally terse — meant for SDRs/SEs to carry into short discovery calls and to hand engineers a minimal tech checklist for a 2–4 week pilot.

Elevator (30s):
We help teams deploy embeddings at production scale with predictable token economics and a safety net for latency spikes. For pilots we recommend using our prefix-KV caching + adaptive batching profile to hit sub-50ms median lookup latencies for common queries and keep cost under baseline.

Ideal pilot profile (quick filter):
- Product: semantic search, RAG with high read-to-write ratio, QA bots with repeat queries
- Traffic: 500–10k monthly queries (pilot), with 5–20% recurring identical queries (cacheable)
- Constraint: need predictable per-query cost and 95thpct latency target <=200ms
- Tech willingness: can run a small webhook to push vectors or integrate via S3/CSV ingest

Qualifying checklist (ask on first call):
- Data: How many documents? (expectation: 10k–1M docs). Are they text-only? Sensitive?
- Query pattern: % of exact-repeat queries? Do users hammer the same top-50 queries?
- Latency SLO: median and 95th targets?
- Cost guardrails: monthly spend cap for pilot? Decision owner for economics?
- Security: need VPC/private deployment or hosted with DLP?

Quick tech checklist for integration handoff (copy to eng):
- Ingest: provide a sample export (5–10 example docs + canonical IDs) or S3 path
- Embedding model: recommend starting with rwd-embed-1-small for cost; can switch to higher fidelity later
- Caching strategy: enable prefix KV caching for repeated queries; set TTL=24h for first pass
- Batching: use our SDK batch_write/lookup helpers; start with batch_size=64 and adjust if latency spikes
- Fallbacks: plan a cheap model fallback route (rwd-embed-1-small -> rwd-embed-1-tiny or token-limited generative fallback)
- Observability: wire route to Console trace view + include top-queries sample set for quality monitoring

Pilot success metrics (OKR-style):
- P0: embedding throughput at target latency (95th <=200ms) and <=X cost/query (negotiated)
- P1: Search/QA relevance: precision@5 >= customer_baseline + 10% or NDCG uplift > 0.08
- P2: Operational: <1 production incident, automated alerts on cache miss surge

Pricing & negotiation plays (short scripts):
- If buyer cites cost sensitivity: pitch reserved capacity discount for steady traffic + intelligent batch/caching to reduce unit cost by 30% in pilot
- If buyer wants fast time-to-value: offer 'Pilot Fast Start' (2-week onboarding + dedicated SE hours) in exchange for a 3-month evaluation commitment

Common objections + soundbites (for sellers):
- "We already use another provider for embeddings" -> "Great — we can run a side-by-side with the same embed model and show the per-query latency and cost delta with caching in 10 days."
- "We can't route PII to hosted services" -> "We have Private deployment (VPC) playbooks and can sign an NDA; many banks started with our on-prem pilot package."
- "We worry about cold-cache latency spikes" -> "We recommend a graded pre-warm: seed cache with top-100 queries during onboarding and enable adaptive batching to smooth tail latency."

Canary / fallback flow (engineer-friendly):
1) Route 10% traffic to Redwood Hosted -> observe latency, hit-rate, and costs for 72 hours
2) If hit-rate < expected: seed cache and increase write-through for hot keys
3) If 95th latency > SLO: auto-fallback to lower-capacity model variant + alert customer; escalate if persistent

Enablement slide outline (5 slides, 5–7 min):
1) Problem + pilot goals (what we will measure)
2) Architecture diagram (ingest -> embed -> index -> cache -> query)
3) Expected economics: example cost breakdown with and without caching
4) Rollout plan + success criteria (2-week milestones)
5) Next steps + required artifacts from customer

Battlecard cheats (sound-bite snippets for quick copy/paste):
- "We cut repeat-query costs by up to 40% using our prefix cache and adaptive batching — customers see ROI inside a month."
- "Fallbacks guarantee continuity: if our primary route gets saturated we automatically serve a compatible model variant and route the remainder to reserved capacity."

Risks & open questions (notes to self):
- Need clearer numbers for small-embeds cost baseline across regions (ask infra for up-to-date unit rates).
- Confirm whether 'seed cache' counts against initial ingestion quota in billing model.
- Verify Private deployment SLA for pilot customers in EU region (legal/regulatory ask).

Tactical play snippets (scripts for SEs):
- Quick demo script (2 min): show a live semantic search before/after cache seed — demonstrate median latency drop and token cost savings on the query panel.
- Email follow-up template (post discovery):
  Subject: Pilot next steps + minimal artifacts we need
  Body: Hi <Name>, thanks for the time. To kick off the pilot we need: sample export (5–10 docs), priority query list (top 50), and your latency/cost targets. We can run setup and a demo within 5 business days.

Next steps (action items):
- [SE] Draft pilot SOW template specific to embeddings pilots (Ethan)
- [Product] Add TTL config example to onboarding docs (Sofia)
- [GTM] Build one-pager for reserved capacity economics (Nora)

Notes: keep this concise and paste-friendly for Slack. This is an iterative draft — expect to prune after first three pilots.

---
Appendix: quick debug checklist for on-call engineers:
- Check cache hit-rate dashboard (Console -> model_route -> cache/hitrate)
- Correlate spike times with batch size changes or upstream traffic patterns
- If memory pressure observed on GPUs: scale down batch_size and spin up a small extra worker pool
- Contact info: eng-oncall@redwood.ai and pilot-se@redwood.ai

End of doc.
